<!-- Generated by genclidocs from the cobra command tree in client/cmd. Do not edit. -->

The ssoossh client turns a browser sign-in into a short-lived SSH certificate. ssh runs it for you, from ssh_config: it generates a fresh keypair, sends the public key to the ssoossh server, opens your browser so you can sign in and approve, and loads the signed certificate into your ssh-agent, or writes key files when there is no agent. Private keys never leave this machine, and a valid certificate is reused until it expires. It also answers sshd's AuthorizedPrincipalsCommand on hosts (`host`) and gets certificates for unattended jobs (`service`).

Start with `ssoossh ssh config`, which prints the ssh_config lines to add.

Configuration is read from /etc/ssoossh/ssoossh.yaml, then ~/.config/ssoossh.yaml, then the file named by --config (on Windows, %ProgramData%\ssoossh\ssoossh.yaml and %AppData%\ssoossh\ssoossh.yaml). Flags override the files, except for settings an administrator has locked. -v traces what a command does; --debug prints the resolved settings and where each one came from.

Documentation: https://mnestor.github.io/ssoossh/

## Synopsis

```
ssoossh [command] [flags]
```

## Options

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `-c`, `--config` | string |  | path to an extra config file, merged after the standard locations |
| `--server` | string |  | server address, e.g. https://ssh.example.com; https is assumed when no scheme is given |
| `-v`, `--verbose` | count | `0` | trace what the command is doing, to stderr; repeat for more (-v steps, -vv requests and files, -vvv bodies) |
| `--version` | bool | `false` | print the version and exit (the same as `ssoossh version`) |

| Command | Description |
| --- | --- |
